findings.reason: The authentic original tiles and frozen source contain no diagram. A concrete pair of sample-path graphs materially clarifies the two quantifier orders: a fixed outcome produces an isolated nonzero point, whereas each fixed time has a singleton null exceptional outcome. The open zero point also prevents the misleading interpretation of a spike as a vertical line segment. This is warranted explanatory diagram scope, not a claim that the existing independent proof was incomplete.
findings.action: Appended a final Remarks section containing paired X/Y path graphs for a fixed interior outcome, open/filled-point conventions, and a caption explaining fixed-time exceptional sets and endpoint behavior.

correction: Added only final Remarks text and one fenced TikZ diagram. First local capture revealed truncated bottom captions; final source adds an explicit bounding box and larger label scale, verified in a second native preview.

diagram_math_checks.objects: For each fixed outcome omega in (0,1), the paths t -> X_t(omega) and t -> Y_t(omega) are maps [0,1] -> R.
diagram_math_checks.check: Statement gives X identically zero and Y equal to the singleton indicator because U(omega)=omega. Both panels use the same time interval, with t=0 and t=1 included; the illustrative omega location is an arbitrary interior position, not an extra condition on the theorem.
The horizontal zero graph includes the full closed interval, including t=omega and the two filled endpoint marks. Its continuity label is exactly step 1.2.

The graph contains (t,0) for every t distinct from omega, excludes (omega,0) with a background-filled open ring, and includes the isolated filled point (omega,1). No vertical edge is drawn, so no unsupported intermediate values are asserted. The included t=0 and t=1 points have value zero for the displayed interior omega.

When omega is 0 or 1, the missing zero point and included value-one point are at that endpoint. The statement still concerns relative-domain continuity; step 1.2 supplies explicit nearby points from within [0,1] for both endpoints and for interior omega. The picture does not replace this epsilon-delta argument.
diagram_math_checks.local_basis: Step 1.2 separately treats omega<1 (including zero) and omega=1.

diagram_math_checks.check: At fixed t, unequal outcomes form exactly {t}, null by F1; hence each fixed-time equality event has probability one. At fixed omega, t=omega gives X=0 and Y=1, so every outcome fails simultaneous equality. These facts explain modification versus indistinguishability using the read local definition and are not inferred from drawing or area.
